headline: P0114 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share is elevated in every complexity stratum, including low-complexity patients; pattern consistent with upcoding
rationale: This provider billed 99215 on 19.2% of 239 claims. The expected share given their patients' complexity is 3.7% (risk-adjusted score 4.72, z vs peers 2.11). The excess is not limited to sicker patients. On patients with 0 chronic conditions, 99215 share is 10.5% vs 2.1% for all providers. With 1 condition it is 11.8% vs 3.4%. Together these two strata account for 12 of the 46 99215s across 106 visits. In the sampled low-complexity claims, several 99215s carry only simple acute diagnoses: upper respiratory infection J06.9 (C0055395, C0055533) and unspecified abdominal pain R10.9 (C0055400, C0055495). Others list a single stable chronic code, such as hyperlipidemia E78.5 (C0055625) and obesity E66.9 (C0055466). The high-complexity 99215s (for example C0055433, C0055590) look more plausible, though shares in those strata are also 2-3x peers. Because the elevation is uniform rather than concentrated in complex patients, sicker patients do not fully explain it. The packet holds no clinical documentation (MDM, time, notes), so medical necessity cannot be judged from claims alone.
next_steps: Request medical records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., C0055395, C0055533, C0055400, C0055495, C0055625, C0055466) and audit MDM or total time against 2021+ E/M guidelines.
Check whether time-based billing is documented for 99215 visits with simple diagnoses (J06.9, R10.9).
Review a sample of high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0055433, C0055590) to confirm the documentation supports high-level MDM, since those strata are also above peers.
Look at the full claim population, not just the samples, for the distribution of diagnoses on 99215s and for repeated 99215s on the same patients (e.g., P0114-N0024, P0114-N0022).
Compare 99214 usage (145 of 239 claims) against peers to check for a broader upward shift in the level mix.
